criteria.extend_compiler_head: Revise runtime/platform/html.ts outside the worker's lane so the compiler-owned head includes the paired script, pushing the pairing through createHTML and emitted state setup. All script bytes would originate in head-owned rendering, at the expense of crossing lanes and revising a factory signature.
criteria.inject_document: For a paired active build, the server response path places one `<script type="module" src="<report-selected digest URL>">` just ahead of `</body>` in text/html documents. Fragment bodies lacking that marker, other media types, HEAD responses, and unpaired builds all retain identical bytes.
criteria.serve_bytes_only: Publish the verified JS/map/table payloads and log the picked URL in the report while binding no page inside UP18, postponing page binding. The narrowest edit, but it leaves the stated pages-receive-the-URL criterion open.

page_binding.instructions: What delivery path should place the report-selected paired script URL into served pages, considering Can cannot author script tags and html.ts belongs to another lane?

criteria.carry_forward: Re-embed each displaced digest byte in successive server generations and note when displacement happened inside the emitted table. Each generation would stand alone, but concrete clock readings in hashed output defeat identical rebuilds, and reusing the prior publish instant understates true replacement age.
criteria.durable_ledger: Hold displaced bytes in a dist-scoped content-addressed pool (dist/assets/<digest><ext>) and note every route's displacement instant in a ledger file replaced atomically (dist/assets.json). A route answers while now minus replacedAt remains inside seven days; builds sweep lapsed rows while holding the project lock, and generations carry no clock data.
criteria.pin_generations: Preserve retired server generations to answer their routes, restricting pruning by age. No extra pool is introduced, yet request handling must discover bytes across generations and might leak staged generations that never went live.

retention.instructions: Which approach preserves displaced digest URLs for seven days minimum across restart, cleanup, and concurrent builds while keeping identical rebuilds intact?

criteria.full_reaudit: Recompute browserBuildId over the manifest files array, verify each file hash from generation bytes read fresh, validate the generation manifest.json cross-link, repeat the entire post-bundle AuditBundle (references, map pairing, table integrity, canaries, prohibited operations), equate lock and lockedInstances with the server graph, plus re-read every browser input directly ahead of atomic selection.
criteria.hashes_and_lock_only: Recompute browserBuildId, verify all file hashes, and equate lock with lockedInstances, while relying on the browser build's prior audit for references, map pairing, table integrity, and canaries instead of duplicating that work in the server build.

verify_scope.instructions: Which verification depth should govern the supplied browser manifest before its paired set goes live?

state.browser_output: Each verified browser generation contains browser/browser.js (entry with the standard `//# sourceMappingURL=browser.js.map` suffix), browser/browser.js.map, diagnostics/table.json, and browser/manifest.json. The manifest record (schemaVersion 1, kind can.browser-manifest) states browserBuildId (SHA-256 spanning the can-browser-bundle-v1 domain and files array), entry, table, path plus sha256 plus route rows per file, toolchain, inputs, lock, and lockedInstances. Published routes match /__can/assets/<sha256>.js alongside .js.map and .json variants. Generation payloads are content-addressed and unchanging, and dist/builds/<id>/manifest.json secures every file digest.
state.mandate: No external users depend on Can, hence backwards compatibility imposes nothing. UP18 attaches a verified browser bundle to a Bun server build using `canlc build --target bun --browser-manifest <file> <server-project>`. Server construction validates the browser build ID, shared locked snapshot, asset graph, and each hash, stores the exact browser build ID and digests within its verified report, and installs the complete matched asset collection in one atomic step; broken rebuilds keep the previous collection. Advise on mechanism from this evidence alone. You have no source access and no execution ability.
state.ownership: The worker's remit spans compiler/main.go, driver build/report/output inputs, runtime/platform/assets.ts, runtime/platform/server.ts, and confined asset/entry tweaks inside compiler/internal/emit (flagged when handed off). compiler/internal/check remains practically closed, runtime/platform/html.ts is a separate lane's asset, and runtime/catalogue.ts is the coordinator's. Any route needing a fresh Can operation, catalogue entry, checker alteration, or html.ts alteration breaches a boundary.
state.page_constraint: Authored JavaScript faces a double bar: project Snapshot turns away .js/.map manifest assets, while the HTML author tag set offers no script tag (only img accepts src). Full Can pages terminate with </body></html>; action fragments never include that marker. Current CSP already mandates script-src 'self' sans inline script and sans unsafe-eval, so an src-only same-origin module tag passes unmodified.
state.race_duty: Validation has to anchor the precise bytes that publish: browser files might mutate between validation and publishing while simultaneous builds vie for the dist. Report plus full asset table install as one unit, and failed validation retains the earlier verified collection untouched. Builds already serialize on an exclusive project lock and rename outputs into place atomically.
state.retention_duty: Displaced digest URLs must continue returning identical bytes no fewer than seven days following displacement, tolerating server restart, prune-like cleanup, and simultaneous builds. Matching inputs must reproduce matching bytes because identity hashes content. Clock readings baked into generations shatter that property; changeable dist records like current.json remain outside hashed content.
state.server_output: Server generations fix the $canAssetTable JSON ({htmx, project[]}) within program/state.ts and place asset payloads under assets/<digest>/<name>. dist/current.json designates the live generation in a single indivisible write. Asset handling responds solely to literal table routes, revalidates the content digest per response, and applies the common content-security-policy throughout.
